newsitem.title: UK: European shares weather U.S. rate rise, spike up.
newsitem.headline: European shares weather U.S. rate rise, spike up.

text.p: European stock markets held on to most of their gains on Wednesday after shrugging off a rise in U.S. interest rates and hints of further U.S. monetary tightening.
The dollar also traded not far from its overnight highs after U.S. economic data showed durable goods orders rose 1.5 percent to a record high in February.
The dollar-boosting figures followed Tuesday's decision of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-making open market committee to increase rates by a quarter of a percentage point.

U.S. Treasury bonds fell in the wake of the strong goods data, however. The figures also weighed down early share trading on Wall Street with the Dow Jones index showing a seven point deficit after the first 30 minutes of business.

British government gilts opened 14/32 lower with Treasuries, but they regained their poise after the unexpected success of a Bank of England auction of 2.5 billion pounds ($4 billion) worth of 10-year bonds.
Traders said the market had been hurt at first by Fed comments accompanying the rate rise that hinted at further monetary tightening at the May meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).
"It has made the market reassess the future of monetary policy. I think another rate rise pretty soon is now being contemplated," said one trader in London.
Despite that, European equity markets reacted with relief that the pre-emptive U.S. strike against inflationary pressures was out of the way.
The region's biggest bourses in London, Paris and Frankfurt put on sharp gains in the morning, but retreated from their highs following the U.S. goods data and Wall Street's weak start.
German shares made the most progress, the 30-share DAX index jumping more than two percent by the close of floor trade as bank shares came back into vogue.

Dealers cited rumours of possible takeovers in the banking industry, fuelled by the tantalising glimpse of a hostile takeover bid furnished by last week's now abandoned bid by steel group Krupp AG for rival Thyssen .
In London, the blue chip FTSE 100 index rose more than one percent in the morning, but retreated from its highs as Wall Street turned lower.
Dealers and analysts said they expected investors to focus more on domestic factors now that the Fed tightening is out of the way.
"We still have our own situation to take on board, the end of the first quarter, a long weekend and the likelihood of a rate rise soon after the (May 1) election," one dealer said.

Shares in leading retailers helped to fuel the early rise as Next Plc posted strong annual results and produced a positive trading statement, dealers said. Next shares were up 25-1/2p at 621-1/2 by 1500 GMT.
French stocks extended their gains through the morning, boosted by shares expected to benefit from a rise in the dollar and strong corporate results.
But the blue-chip CAC-40 index followed the trend of Europe's other big bourses by retreating from its highs in the afternoon to stand about 0.75 percent higher.
On the foreign exchange market, the dollar traded just off its highs after being boosted by the U.S. rate rise, the prospect of a future tightening and the durable goods data.

"The tone for the dollar after the rate rise is pretty positive, though the quarter point hike was already priced in," said Jeremy Hawkins at Bank of America. "The fact we've had higher rates cemented now helps underline the divergence between the U.S. economic cycle and continental Europe."

Analysts said the dollar remained vulnerable to asset market sell-offs because of the amount of foreign investment in dollar securities, which is needed to fund the large U.S. current account deficit.
CURRENCIES AT 1500 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6949 marks and 124.33 yen compared with 1.6919 marks and 123.92 yen in late European trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1500 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 27.9, or 0.65 percent, at 4,298.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index was up 18.38 points, or 0.7 percent, at 2,642.63.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 68.98 points, or 2.06 percent, at 3,418.12. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index was up 46.47, or 1.38 percent, at 3,421.4.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $346.05 versus $346.80 in the morning. Silver was up once cent at $5.14.
